question.text:
Find the least-squares slope b of the line y = a + bx fitted to (0, 1), (1, 0), (2, 2).
(A) 0 (B) 1/3 (C) 1/2 (D) 2/3 (E) 1

solution.text:
The normal equations are 3a + 3b = 3 and 3a + 5b = 4. Subtraction gives 2b = 1. Therefore
the slope is 1/2 and the intercept is 1/2.

question.text:
2
A real matrix P satisfies P = P. Which additional condition is equivalent to P being an
orthogonal projection?
(A) det P = 0.
(B) tr P is an integer.
(C) All eigenvalues of P are real.
(D) ∥Px∥ ≤ ∥x∥ for every real vector x, in the Euclidean norm.
(E) P is diagonalizable over R.

solution.text:
An orthogonal projection is contractive by the orthogonal decomposition and the
Pythagorean theorem. Conversely, let u ∈ im P and v ∈ ker P . Contractivity applied
2 2
to u + tv gives ∥u∥ ≤ ∥u + tv∥ for every real t. The linear coefficient 2⟨u, v⟩ must vanish,
so range and kernel are orthogonal. The other listed spectral properties do not distinguish
oblique idempotents.
